note: Possibilities to raise with a clinician, for a patient with a knee complaint and no procedure. These are NOT a diagnosis and carry no probability. The engine matches on symptoms only; the more_likely_if and less_likely_if lines are shown to the patient as things a clinician can tell apart, and are never evaluated by the software.
disclaimer: This is a list of things worth asking about. It is not a diagnosis, and it is not ordered by how likely anything is.

conditions.name: Osteoarthritis of the knee
conditions.plain: Wear of the cartilage that cushions the joint.
more_likely_if: it came on gradually over months or years rather than suddenly
it is stiff for less than half an hour when you wake up
it is worse after activity and at the end of the day
you are over 50, or there is arthritis in the family
less_likely_if: it started suddenly after a twist or an injury
the knee locks completely and will not straighten
conditions.next_step: A GP assessment, usually with a weight-bearing X-ray. Most people start with exercise, weight management and pain relief.

conditions.name: Meniscus (cartilage) tear
conditions.plain: A tear in one of the two rubbery pads that sit between the bones.
more_likely_if: it started with a twist, a squat or a pivot
the knee catches, clicks or locks on you
swelling came on over a day rather than within minutes
the pain is along the line of the joint, at the side
less_likely_if: there was no injury and the ache has been there for years
conditions.next_step: A GP or physiotherapy assessment. An MRI only if it does not settle, because many tears are managed without surgery.

conditions.name: Patellofemoral pain (pain around the kneecap)
conditions.plain: Irritation where the kneecap runs against the thigh bone.
more_likely_if: the pain is at the front, around or behind the kneecap
it is worse on stairs and hills, or after sitting a long time
there is no real swelling
it started after a change in how much you were walking or training
less_likely_if: the knee locks or gives way
the knee is hot and visibly swollen
conditions.next_step: Physiotherapy is usually the first and often the only treatment needed.

conditions.name: Ligament sprain or tear
conditions.plain: A stretch or tear of one of the bands that hold the knee steady.
more_likely_if: you heard or felt a pop at the time
it swelled within a few hours of the injury
the knee feels like it will buckle under you
it happened in sport, or in a fall
less_likely_if: there was no injury at all
conditions.next_step: Assessment the same week by a GP or a sports clinic. Some of these need surgery and some do not.

conditions.name: Bursitis in front of the kneecap
conditions.plain: Swelling of the small fluid sac that sits over the kneecap.
more_likely_if: there is a soft, squashy swelling right over the kneecap
you kneel a lot for work or at home
the joint itself still bends more or less normally
less_likely_if: the whole joint is swollen and you cannot bend it
conditions.next_step: A GP visit - and the same day if it is hot, red, or you have a fever, because an infected bursa is treated quickly.

conditions.name: Gout or another inflammatory arthritis
conditions.plain: Inflammation driven by crystals or by the immune system rather than by wear.
more_likely_if: it came on over hours and is very painful even to touch
the skin over it is red and hot
you have had gout before, or in another joint like the big toe
you are stiff for more than an hour in the mornings
less_likely_if: it built up slowly over years with no flares
conditions.next_step: A GP appointment. A blood test, and sometimes drawing a little fluid from the joint, tells these apart.

conditions.name: Baker's cyst
conditions.plain: A pocket of joint fluid that bulges out at the back of the knee.
more_likely_if: there is a bulge behind the knee
it feels tight at the back when you bend it
you already have arthritis or a cartilage problem in that knee
less_likely_if: the swelling is at the front of the knee
conditions.next_step: A GP assessment. Worth knowing: a cyst that bursts can look exactly like a clot in the calf, which is why calf swelling always gets checked properly.

conditions.name: Patellar tendinopathy
conditions.plain: Irritation of the tendon just below the kneecap.
more_likely_if: the pain is in one spot just below the kneecap
it is worse with jumping, running or stairs
it is tender when you press that exact spot
it started after you increased your training
less_likely_if: the knee is swollen and hot
the pain is deep inside the joint rather than on the front
conditions.next_step: Physiotherapy, and easing the load for a while rather than stopping completely.
